mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC over any 2-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signal weakening demand in housing and retail sectors, depressing corporate earnings and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline >1% monthly, or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 during late-cycle expansion signals supply chain disruptions that squeeze corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0 and late-cycle expansion conditions hold, or Rank IC for signal in regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high GDP level (GDPC1) above 18,000 billion signals robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when GDPC1 > 18,000, or Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL annualized change) above 2.5% signals imminent monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized change > 2.5%, or Rank IC over any 2-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises >0.2pp, or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC for signal in tightening regime is below 0.03.
